Name: Individual
Notes on definition: An individual operating under a trading name (a 'sole trader') should be regarded as an individual rather than an organisation. But their trading status can be captured as a role using XP1.

Name: Family
Definition: Humans in a family relationship with each other, whether legally formalised (e.g. marriage, civil partnership, registered as parent, adoption) or not. Includes unmarried couples

Name: Corporate body
Definition: A private, commercial, charitable or not-for-profit entity other than a human which has legal personality and is not part of the state or other public body.

Name: Unincorporated body
Definition: A group of humans with some shared interest, not formalised into a corporate body. This may include traditional communities or charitable / not-for-profit groups. It may also include commercial groups, whether or not with specific legal incidents (e.g. joint liability of partners in an unincorporated partnership).
Notes on definition: Families or corporate bodies are excluded from this concept.
Examples: Some general partnerships and clubs, though this depends on applicable law

Name: Authority
Definition: A state, international or other body carry out a public or similar (e.g. professional standards) function and exercises governmental or administrative power.
Notes on definition: There is inevitably some scope for argument at the edges as to the line between a public entity / authority and the other types of organisation. Different legal systems may draw the line differently. However, the basic distinction is widely recognised.

Name: Land and buildings
Definition: Land, buildings and any interests in or relating to them (e.g. leases, licences, rights of way, mortgages)

Name: Tangible property
Definition: Physical things which can be owned, and which are not land or buildings

Name: Intangible property
Definition: Anything of a non-physical nature in which property rights are recognised. Includes documents representing such rights.
Examples: Intellectual property, patent, copyright, trade mark, trademark, trade-mark, share, debt portfolio, debenture, derivative, bank account, financial instrument, bill of lading, thing in action, chose in action, crypto asset, cryptocurrency, non-fungible token, NFT

Name: Contracts
Notes on definition: Documents and other artifacts containing contract terms are addressed separately

Name: Non-contractual obligation
Definition: Legal rights and duties of a private law nature, other than those incidental to personal relationships (par-ppl), property (par-pty) or contract (par-obg-1)
Notes on definition: Although contract is a well-recognised concept across legal systems, other types of private obligation are harder to map between systems. We suggest this as a useful category to start with - it can be subdivided later if found helpful to do so.

Name: Public obligation
Definition: Powers of public or quasi-public authorities and officials, and the rights and duties arising between people and organisations (on the one hand) and such authorities or officials.
